note: Phase 6 closes 2 of its 433 function rows and none of its 531 data objects. The closed rows are the two exported joint-descriptor rows, and each is closed by the one thing the schema accepts: a mutation aimed at it that a registered gate caught. The target that catches them is NxPhysicsJointTests as a STAGED-PAIR differential -- not an oracle differential, because an oracle differential runs only against the pinned DLL and so can never catch a mutation to the candidate (recorded in evidence 11l). The deferred rows are the ones Phase 6 has not reconstructed, which is a debt rather than an obstruction.

proof_kinds.differential_falsified: a mutation aimed at this row in a throwaway `git archive` copy, rebuilt, and run against the committed oracle transcript through a REGISTERED STAGED-PAIR target. The gate catches it because the target loads the rebuilt module and the runner compares the two transcripts line for line.
proof_kinds.static_proof_falsified: a mutation aimed at the row and caught by a static check rather than a differential. Phase 6 has none.

deferred_reasons.not_reconstructed_in_phase: Phase 6 did not reconstruct this row and names nothing that blocks it. A debt, not an obstruction.
deferred_reasons.reconstructed_not_falsified: the row is reconstructed and carries a recorded proof, but no mutation has been aimed at it. This is the work Phase 6 has left: 129 rows, each needing one mutation and one measured detection.
deferred_reasons.data_object_not_dispositioned: no closure schema lets any phase close a data object, so the data half arrives here by construction.

entry_points: NxJointDesc_SetGlobalAnchor (0x000980b0) and NxJointDesc_SetGlobalAxis (0x000982e0), resolved by GetProcAddress against the staged pair -- both are exported, which is what makes a staged-pair target possible for these rows
the census rows Phase 6 owns, by rva
differentials: NxPhysicsJointTests, registered as a Phase 6 STAGED-PAIR differential: four revolute cases, each building the descriptor, creating the joint, reading the anchor, the axis, the actors and the state back, and releasing. The oracle and candidate transcripts are identical after the runner normalises the pair-identity lines, and four coverage assertions are registered against them, so a mutation that moves any of those lines fails the gate.
NxPhysicsJointDescTests, registered as a Phase 6 ORACLE differential: the two exported descriptor rows over four cases.

falsification.mutation: Re-measured by joint-open-items Task 4 after Task 4 rewrote this row's body from the listing (the earlier text quoted `m[0] * dx + m[3] * dy + m[6] * dz`, which no longer exists: the transform is now the shared helper nxJointTransposeMultiply, and the matrix composition the shared nxJointWorldMatrix). The mutation is aimed at code only this row has, its anchor difference: in a throwaway `git archive` copy of HEAD 19251a2+aac77f1 (D:/FlamingEnt__/novodex-analysis/t4mut), `const float dz = static_cast<float>(static_cast<double>(wsAnchor.z) - t[2]);` in NxJointDesc_SetGlobalAnchor became `... - t[1]);`. The copy was configured and built (NxFoundation, NxPhysics, NxPhysicsJointStagedPairTests) and run through run_phase_gate.ps1 -Phase 7 with that copy as RepoRoot/BuildRoot. CAUGHT: `differential target=NxPhysicsJointStagedPairTests oracle_exit=0 candidate_exit=0 stdout_delta=320`, and the registered assertion `case=revolute index=10 saved anchor0=c03fffff.3f800000.3f800001 anchor1=40044444.406aaaaa.bf91110f` failed (the mutant printed anchor0=bffffffe.3f800000.3f800000 anchor1=3f888889.40b55555.3f5ddde6). Only the rotated fixture catches it: the identity fixture's actors sit at t.y = t.z = 0, so its registered lines did not move. Restored (the copy's JointDesc.cpp byte-identical to HEAD again), rebuilt and re-run: stdout_delta=0, coverage_assertions_evaluated=103 floor=103, phase_gate=7 status=pass. Also measured and NOT caught: rounding dx to float (`const double dx = static_cast<float>(...)`) left stdout_delta=0, because on every registered input the float difference is already exact; the row's register-precision dx is therefore reproduced from the listing but not pinned by a transcript.

Re-measured by joint-open-items Task 4 after Task 4 rewrote this row's body from the listing (the earlier mutation, `axis.x * inv * 1.5`, was measured on the float-length transcription; the earlier claim that the two rows are independently falsifiable predates the shared nxJointWorldMatrix/nxJointTransposeMultiply helpers, so it is re-established here with a mutation in code only this row has, its normalisation). In the same throwaway copy, `if(length != 0.0)` in NxJointDesc_SetGlobalAxis became `if(length > 1.0)`, so no axis shorter than 1 is normalised. Rebuilt and run through run_phase_gate.ps1 -Phase 7 as above. CAUGHT: `stdout_delta=3655` (non-unit axes now fail desc.isValid(), so createJoint returns null and the transcript loses lines), and the registered assertion `case=revolute index=3 out_anchor=40000000.40800000.00000000 out_axis=3f13cd3a.3f13cd3a.3f13cd3a state=0` failed. Restored and re-run: stdout_delta=0, phase_gate=7 status=pass. Also measured and NOT caught: rounding the length to float (`static_cast<float>(sqrt(...))`, what the pre-Task-4 transcription did) left stdout_delta=0; the register-precision length is reproduced from the listing (0x982f9-0x98326) but no registered input separates it. With the anchor mutation above, each row is caught by a mutation in its own code and neither mutation touches the shared helpers.
